review: heat-exposure-trial@1 adds one general operation, heat-exposure-trial (learning 2, 0.2 energy per study round), registered last for this run's scope, with modes inspect, sample, compare, inspect-progress, resume and cancel and parameters targetId (an exact visible object or item through the shared resolver), x and y (a visible point within 5), baselineId (an exact own trial record) and sampleRounds (1-3, default 1). Located thermal code, reused and not changed: forestClimate (forest-climate.ts, foundation-forest@1) gives the air at a point from season, weather, daylight, the ground kind (rocky -3, wet bank -1.5, forest floor +0.5, other +1.5), the climate offset and the seasonal pressure, lowers outdoor air by 0.6 x (rain + wind), and only inside an enclosure interior (v7Interior: the caves, buffering 0.72 toward 12, or another enclosure's buffering) changes air and light; forestPhysiology (forest-environment.ts, foundation-forest@1), applied once per round by v7Physiology from v7Step, moves body temperature by 0.035 x (air - body) / (1 + insulation) through shelterTemperature (forest-thermal.ts), with the insulation of enclosing objects or the person, the installed refuge, lean-to, simple, shared, branch-screen and weather-shelter hooks, worn insulation and fire rules, and heat damage above 34. No object without an enclosure (trees, plants, rocks, fallen branches) enters either function, so the model has no shade, sun load or obstruction resolver; this release ships the measured occupied-position precursor, never reports shade, and leaves shelter effectiveness beyond enclosure interiors as an explicit development dependency. inspect (1 round, 0.2) reports the person's body temperature and this round's air, indoor flag, light, rain, wind, daylight, season and ground at their position (measured), and model-derived insulation, enclosure, next-round body temperature, the share of installed shelter or fire rules, and the same-round open-soil value; with no target it surveys the nearest visible standing spot of each other ground kind and each visible enclosure interior (at most 6), with a target or point only that one, each with distance, standing, air difference and next-round body change, labelled model-derived and nothing measured there; a named object without an enclosure is reported as no represented protection, an enclosure with its visible geometry and entrances. sample takes 0.2 per paid round only where the person stands and records at each round start the body temperature, health and readings (measured), the prediction and the open-soil reference (model-derived); the after reading is the body temperature at the start of the next round, taken by the next action or the environment step before that round's update, free; a trial completes when every requested sample is measured and is labelled against the open-soil reference and against baselineId or the previous record. compare (1 round, 0.2) uses no sample; inspect-progress costs 1 round and 0.2; cancel 1 round and no energy; every refusal comes before any cost. Modeling assumptions: predictions run forestPhysiology on a discarded copy of the round's world with the person placed at the point, so the world keeps exactly one body-heat update per round and adds no cooling; readings at the person's position are this round's climate, the values the next observation shows, and are labelled measured, while values elsewhere are computed from visible ground and geometry and labelled model-derived, never measured; body temperature changes only in that update, so the next-round-start reading is exactly the sampled round's result, and tests show it equals both the prediction and the restated law; the open-soil reference is the nearest centre of an open ordinary soil cell the person sees or remembers, outside every enclosure and clear of solid footprints, with the same round and starting body temperature, or unknown if none; differences below 0.001 per round count as none; lower heat exposure than open ordinary soil needs both the model-derived site value and the measured after reading below the open-soil value; two records at different rounds give an observed trend only, and a position-to-position exposure claim needs a lower model-derived site difference and a lower measured contrast, each against its own same-round reference; the body label follows only the measured sign (cooling only when body temperature fell, otherwise slower warming, not cooling); insulation slows warming and cooling alike, so a cool insulated interior can cool a warmer body less per round than cool open ground, and the labels follow the numbers; a resumed segment must be within 0.1 of the trial position and interrupted rounds are separate segments; a new sample while a trial is paused stops it as replaced; the latest 4 trial records and the latest inspection and comparison are kept. Lifecycle: another action, moving away or energy below 0.2 pause before the next charge, health below 20 or body temperature outside 7-34 stop it (conservative activity guards, not a diagnosis), death ends it and a reading still due stays unknown; nothing is refunded or reserved and no material is used. No reward: no satisfaction rule, no qualified flag, no top-level progress, elapsed or remaining number, no knowledge record, no buff, health or comfort change beyond the existing update, and no object is made. Visuals: no components; every event carries view metadata (actor, work, mode, tick, location, site, status, sample counts, exact targets, provenance, evidence status, no badge), attention only on performed work, and a protection overlay only on a completed trial inside a represented enclosure whose lower exposure is supported. Every earlier package is byte-identical by an id@version hash assertion, foundation-forest@1 and foundation-open@1 included. In this world at round 197 Moss stands on open ordinary soil at about (15.55, 17.62) with body temperature 30.92 and energy 40 at night in rain (0.88); the next round's air there is 28.39 and the body cools by about 0.089 per round; the forest floor 1.37 west (air 1 lower) gives about -0.124 and the wet bank 2.95 east (air 3 lower) about -0.194 per round; canopy-69 and the other trees change nothing; neither cave is in Moss's view or memory: cave-2 at (6, 29), 14.9 away with its doorway at (6, 31), has interior air 16.46 and insulation 2 (about -0.169 per round), and cave-1 at (35, 8), 21.7 away, interior air 15.48 (about -0.18); walking costs about 2 energy per unit on ordinary ground at 0.8 per round; the model's open-soil air there peaked at 33.3 in round 174 and stays at or below 31 through round 400.
